---
title: "4 Homework: documenting a model, with an agent"
---

Three exercises for Session 4: the first is also the session's lab. In each you direct an
AI coding agent and then check its work against the repository — the same discipline a
validator applies to a developer's document.

**Before you start.** Work on `main` (`git checkout main`), at the repository's root.
Answers go in `wiki/homework/_answers/<ID>.md`, a folder git ignores; drafts of D5 go where
the documentation lives, in `wiki/mdd/adjudication/`. None of the exercises needs Quarto:
the lint and the self-check are plain Python.

```bash
python -m wiki.homework.check <ID>
```

Each solution below was written by running the exercise with an agent (Claude Code) in this
repository, including where its first attempt went wrong. Try the exercise before you open
it.

## H4.1 Draft one part of D5 {#h4-1}

**Kind:** Build. **Prompt card:**
[`workshop/prompt-cards/HW-H4.1.md`](https://github.com/aayancheng/banking-analytics-workshop/blob/main/workshop/prompt-cards/HW-H4.1.md).
**Answer:** `wiki/mdd/adjudication/<part>.qmd`.

**Goal.** Have the agent draft one of the nine parts of the
[template](../mdd/index.qmd#the-template) for D5, Loan Adjudication, starting from the
[chapter's stub](../mdd/adjudication/index.qmd), with [D4](../mdd/score/index.qmd) as the
worked example. In the lab, pairs take different parts and work in parallel; as homework,
finish the chapter.

**Check:** `python -m wiki.homework.check H4.1 --part <part>` checks one part: at least
150 words beyond the template's comment, at least one fact cited, and a clean lint — every
number a fact, every fact resolving. Without `--part` it checks all nine.

**The trap.** A draft that lints clean can still be wrong. A `score.*` fact renders the
scorecard's number, not the adjudication model's; a claim about a cutoff can contradict
`adjudication/src/policy.py`. The lint proves every number is traceable, not that it is the
right number in the right sentence. Read two claims against the code yourself.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Solution"}
**The prompt that worked** is the card, with `performance` as the part.

**The agent's draft** (excerpt, as rendered):

> The gradient-boosted model scores a held-out AUC of {{< var adj.auc >}} on all held-out
> applicants, against a gate of {{< var adj.gate_auc >}}. That is below the scorecard's
> {{< var score.auc_holdout >}} on the same rows, although the model consumes the score as
> one of its {{< var adj.n_features >}} inputs; the difference is inside the scorecard's own
> interval of ±{{< var score.auc_ci_half >}}, so it is not evidence that either model is
> better.
>
> Calibration by zone, stability and the booked-only AUC need facts that do not exist yet;
> they are added in `wiki/facts/` before this section is written.

**Where it first went wrong.** The first draft defined the lift as measured on the top
fifth of applicants by predicted PD, but wrote the fifth as a percentage. The check failed
it: the lint reports a hand-typed number and names the line. Numbers hide in phrases that read like words. The
agent rephrased; it did not add the literal to `lint_allow.txt`, which would have silenced
the lint and left the number untraceable.

Two things it did right are worth copying. It named the gaps — calibration, stability, the
booked-only AUC for this model — as "not yet measured" rather than filling them. And it
compared the two models only within the precision the scorecard's bootstrap interval allows.

**Rehearsed.** A line reading "The AUC is" followed by the adjudication AUC typed as digits
fails the check with "hand-typed number". So does a relaxed gate in `score/src/train.py`,
in every exercise.
:::

## H4.2 Turn the agent into a validator {#h4-2}

**Kind:** Audit. **Prompt card:**
[`workshop/prompt-cards/HW-H4.2.md`](https://github.com/aayancheng/banking-analytics-workshop/blob/main/workshop/prompt-cards/HW-H4.2.md).
**Answer:** `wiki/homework/_answers/H4.2.md`.

**Goal.** Have the agent review D4 as an independent validator, *without* reading the
findings D4 raises about itself, and write at least three findings about the model, each
with evidence. Then compare its findings with
[D4.7](../mdd/score/limitations.qmd) — which did it miss, and which did it find that D4.7
does not raise?

**Check:** `python -m wiki.homework.check H4.2` — at least three findings, each citing
evidence that exists: a fact key from `wiki/facts/facts.json` or a path in the repository.

**The trap.** Evidence that is the documentation itself. "The chapter says so" proves what
the document claims, not what the model does. Point at a fact or at code.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Solution"}
**The prompt that worked** is the card as written. The answer's shape:

```text
F1: The gate is met on all held-out applicants but not on the held-out booked applicants,
the population the bank lends to.
Evidence: `score.pop.booked.auc`

F2: A missing input, including a bureau field, is silently scored as zero rather than
refused, although 4.6 shows the model fails its gate without bureau data. The refer rule is
documented but not implemented.
Evidence: `score/src/feature_engineering.py`

F3: Band AAA under-predicts on the held-out booked applicants by a ratio well outside the
monitoring tolerance.
Evidence: `score.band_booked.AAA.ratio`

F4: No out-of-time sample; the PSI between random splits measures sampling noise, not drift.
Evidence: `score.psi_score`
```

**Where it first went wrong.** Its first F3 cited a page anchor in the documentation as
evidence. The check failed it — no such file — and rightly: the evidence for a finding
against the model is the measured ratio, not the page that reports it. It re-pointed F3 at
the fact.

**Against D4.7.** Two of the agent's findings are D4.7's (the gate population, the missing
out-of-time sample). Two are matters D4.7 records only as *observations*: the missing-input
rule and the loose calibration in the top bands. D4.7 argues both are too small, or too
thinly evidenced, to raise on this data — a validator could fairly disagree about the first,
since the control is documented but not built. The agent missed the concentration of the
score in band D and the non-monotonic weight of evidence of `leverage`. Both were on pages
it had been given — band D's share in [4.5](../mdd/score/performance.qmd), the
weight of evidence in [4.4](../mdd/score/assumptions.qmd) — and it missed them by reading
selectively: it worked through performance and sensitivity closely and never opened the
binning tables. An agent audits what it looks at, so ask it which pages and tables it read.

Note too that the blind is partial. Other D4 pages cross-reference the findings by number,
so an agent that reads everything is led towards D4.7's list; an honest review says which
findings it reached independently.
:::

## H4.3 Extend the crosswalk for one module {#h4-3}

**Kind:** Build. **Prompt:** below; there is no card and no self-check. **Answer:**
`wiki/homework/_answers/H4.3.md`.

**Goal.** The [crosswalk](../reference/crosswalk.qmd) maps each element of SR 11-7 to a
part of the documentation — N.1 to N.9 stand for any model chapter. Have the agent make it
concrete for one module: for each row, the page and section of that chapter where the
element is covered, or "not covered in this chapter" with where it is covered instead.

> In the `banking-analytics-workshop` repo on `main`, read `wiki/reference/crosswalk.qmd` and
> every page in `wiki/mdd/score/`. For each row of the crosswalk table, give the D4 page and
> section heading where that element is documented for the Business Credit Score, as a
> relative link from `wiki/reference/`. If D4 does not cover it, say so and name the chapter
> that does. Do not change the OSFI or PRA columns and do not add principle numbers of your
> own. Write the table to `wiki/homework/_answers/H4.3.md`.

**The trap.** Regulatory references from memory. An agent will happily supply principle
numbers, and a wrong one reads exactly like a right one. The crosswalk's numbers were read
from the source documents; the exercise extends the table's *here* column and nothing else.
The second trap is the easy row: a cell filled with the chapter's index page, because
something must go there.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Solution"}
**The agent's table** for D4, the Business Credit Score:

| SR 11-7 element | In D4 |
|---|---|
| Model definition and inventory | [D4, "at a glance"](../mdd/score/index.qmd); the inventory is D0 |
| Purpose and use | [4.1](../mdd/score/purpose.qmd), including [prohibited uses](../mdd/score/purpose.qmd#prohibited-uses) |
| Data | [4.2](../mdd/score/data.qmd), including [leakage controls](../mdd/score/data.qmd#leakage-controls) |
| Model dependencies | [4.1, who consumes it](../mdd/score/purpose.qmd#who-consumes-it-and-how); the dependency map is D3 |
| Conceptual soundness | [4.3](../mdd/score/methodology.qmd), [4.4](../mdd/score/assumptions.qmd) |
| Implementation | [the binning solver](../mdd/score/methodology.qmd#implementation-note-the-binning-solver), [where the gate is asserted](../mdd/score/gate.qmd#where-it-is-asserted); the platform is D9 |
| Performance and outcomes analysis | [4.5](../mdd/score/performance.qmd) |
| Sensitivity | [4.6](../mdd/score/sensitivity.qmd) |
| Limitations | [4.7](../mdd/score/limitations.qmd) |
| Ongoing monitoring | [4.8](../mdd/score/monitoring.qmd) |
| Governance and change control | [4.9](../mdd/score/gate.qmd), including its [history](../mdd/score/gate.qmd#history); sign-off is D11 |
| Risk tiering | not covered in this chapter: D0 |
| AI/ML: explainability, autonomy, agent use | [4.3, why this method](../mdd/score/methodology.qmd#why-this-method) (exact reason codes); agent use is D10 |

**Where it first went wrong.** Its first pass put "model dependencies" down as not covered
in D4 and pointed only at D3. Listing D4's section headings showed otherwise: 4.1 has a
section on who consumes the score and how, which is the score's side of the dependency. It
made the same mistake on the *implementation* row, first answering "D9 only" before finding
the two D4 sections that describe how the scorecard is built and gated in code. Both errors
were the easy row: a plausible cell filled before the headings were read.
:::

## Check your own work

After any exercise, `python verify.py` should still pass. If it does not, the agent changed
something it was told not to: `git status` shows what, and `git checkout -- <path>` puts it
back.
